summary:
Task 5 (auto-install-review-packet) writes one file, docs/planning/v2/PHASE_57_LOCAL_AGENT_REVIEW.md, and the installed self-change policy allows it (assertDiffAllowed returned ok, which I checked against ~/.openclaw/extensions/orion-control/dist/self-development-authority.js:233). Every criterion can be met inside that scope. The problems are about what evidence the worker can actually reach:

(1) The plan file is untracked at HEAD bbe4575 (`git status` shows `?? docs/agentic/plans/advance-orion-capabilities.md`). So the worker cannot read tasks 1–4's acceptance criteria or the plan's "Next batch" list. The brief has to quote them word for word: about 3,825 characters for the 19 criteria and about 1,115 for the next-batch section, inside MAX_BRIEF 18,000 (contract.mjs:64), which is shared with common.md.

(2) The worker has no git access and gets no diffs, receipts or commit ids. renderContract/workerTurn carry none of these (prompts.mjs:43-74, 137-154). Run state lives outside the worktree in ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/project-agent (projects.mjs:10), and readScoped refuses absolute or `..` paths (workspace.mjs:175-176). What it can use: READ the final contents of the two batch files, which are both absent at HEAD, so their whole content is the combined change from tasks 1–4. It can also run ### CHECK.

(3) The only observed test evidence is the tail of the check output shown to the worker, at most 6,000 characters per check (prompts.mjs:104). The existing automation-tests suite prints 6,954 characters on node v26.5.0, so the first ~15 admission test lines are cut. The summary lines (`ℹ tests 82`, `ℹ pass 82`, `ℹ fail 0`) are visible. node-syntax passes without testing anything: it prints "no matching changed files" (checks.mjs:262-264).

(4) The local reviewer sees only the doc diff, the contract with the brief, and pass/fail for each check with the output stripped (reviewer.mjs:83; prompts.mjs:156-168 passes no files). It cannot check the doc's claims against the code.

(5) A runtime limit that matters a lot here: with a single scope file, "progress" is possible only on the first write. After that, every exchange with FILE, CHECK or DONE adds 1 to the stuck counter, and the counter is tested before DONE is handled (worker.mjs:276-277, 342-353; stuckAfterTurns 4 at models.mjs:92). So the worker gets at most three such exchanges, counting the first write, and the third must contain ### DONE. A write longer than 12,000 characters (worker.mjs:280) or a SUBTASK index change (worker.mjs:243-245) forces a self-review exchange where DONE is withheld.

Big files that would blow the ~48,500-token input budget (65536-16000-1024, models.mjs:59,63 and context.mjs:46-55): HANDOFF.md at HEAD is 93,611 characters (cut at 90,000), PHASE_GATES.json is 545,310 characters, AGENTS.md is 47,073 characters. The worker must not READ these, and it cannot read .builds/ because it is gitignored (.gitignore:42).

The doc has to describe what install.mjs actually does. Where the code differs from the earlier contracts, the doc says so rather than restating the contracts. It uses no commit SHAs and no line numbers, because the worker sees files without line numbers (prompts.mjs:91-96). It must never say the real scheduler was used, that anything was installed, or that Phase 57 is complete.

apis.name: automationSchedulePlan
apis.behavior: Pure preview. Throws on validateProposal issues (l.9-11); throws unless action==='agenda_today' and delivery===undefined (l.12-14); throws on invalid timezone/policy (l.16-18), invalid clock (l.19), expiry outside today..180 days in timeZone (l.20-25). Returns {readyToInstall:false, nextGate, name:`orion-auto-${proposal.name}`, timeZone, cron, commandArgv:[join(repoRoot,'scripts/orion-automation-run'), proposal.name], policy:{action,intent,expiresOn,conditions,permissions,riskLimits,failureBehavior}, schedulerArgs:['cron','add','--name',name,'--cron',cron,'--tz',timeZone,'--command-argv',JSON.stringify(commandArgv),'--command-cwd',repoRoot,'--disabled','--exact','--no-deliver','--timeout-seconds','120','--output-max-bytes','4096','--json']} (l.28-39). policy does NOT contain name, trigger, timeZone, installationId or installedAt.

apis.name: initializeAutomationDispatch
apis.behavior: Validates the record via installation() (l.14-27: requires action in AUTOMATION_ACTIONS, failureBehavior in stop|retry_once|report_and_continue, string installationId, trigger daily|hourly|weekly with atMinute/atHour/weekday). Calls initializeAutomationAdmission(join(root,'admission'), record) (l.52), messages ledger only if record.delivery (l.53), then creates join(root, `${sha256hex(installationId)}.dispatch.json`) = {version:1,binding,phase:'ready',lastAt:null,lastSlot:null} with open(...,'wx') so it throws EEXIST rather than overwrite (l.39-49, 54-56).

apis.name: initializeAutomationAdmission
apis.behavior: binding() throws unless name matches /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,47}$/, installationId matches /^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{8,80}$/, valid expiresOn, riskLimits.maxRunsPerDay 1..1440, permissions.expectsMode in contained|guarded|open|sovereign, conditions object, explicit supported IANA timeZone (l.14-41). mkdir root recursive 0o700, writes join(root, `${sha256hex(installationId)}.json`) = {version:1,binding,day:null,runs:0,lastAt:0} with 'wx', then fsyncs the directory (l.62-70).

apis.name: dispatchAutomation
apis.behavior: Returns {status:'refused'|'failed'|'succeeded'|'outcome_unknown', reason?, attempts?, output?, delivery?}. The lock is mkdir `${file}.lock` (l.65-67) and is removed in finally (l.173); a crash leaves it in place. Phases: ready|pending|stopped|action_completed|delivery_pending|delivery_unknown (l.73). Anything other than ready refuses, and pending maps to outcome_unknown (l.78-80). Reservation happens before pending is persisted; a crash between them consumes quota (l.103-108). An unknown result or an uncertified failure goes to stopped and returns outcome_unknown (l.111-118).

apis.name: runInstalledAutomation
apis.signature: async runInstalledAutomation(name, scheduledAt, { automationRoot = join(homedir(), '.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations'), repoRoot = repo, checks = createAutomationHostChecks({repoRoot}), run = executeFile } = {})
apis.behavior: Production defaults (l.19-20). Reads automationRoot/installed/<name>.json (l.25). Requires record.name===name, action==='agenda_today', no delivery, and a parseable installedAt string (l.29-31); otherwise refuses with installation_unavailable_or_unsupported (l.34). Re-reads the record and compares its canonical identity before authorizing and executing (l.35-38, 46, 53, 58). Never initializes ledgers. Dispatches at join(automationRoot,'runtime') (l.77).

apis.name: automationTick
apis.signature: async automationTick(args, { now = Date.now, run = runInstalledAutomation } = {})
apis.behavior: Accepts exactly one valid name, floors the time to the minute, and returns {exitCode, summary:{status, reason?}}. Called by the scheduler entry point scripts/orion-automation-run (l.1-6).

apis.name: removeAutomationSchedule
apis.behavior: The only source evidence of the real scheduler's read format. It runs `cron list --all --json` and expects {jobs:[{id,name,...}], hasMore:false, offset:0, total} (l.9-18). It removes by exact id with `cron remove <id> --json` (l.24) and then re-lists to confirm the job is gone (l.25-28). It establishes nothing about the enabled/cron/tz/argv/cwd/exact/noDeliver fields in the real scheduler's read-back.

apis.name: orion-automation CLI (install/remove)
apis.behavior: install always fails, saying guarded registration is unavailable and nothing was scheduled (l.153-157). ROOT is ~/.openclaw/orion-controlled/automations (l.57). The OpenClaw binary is ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw (l.60). schedule-plan passes repoRoot = ~/Desktop/ORION (l.148). There is no enable/activate command anywhere.

apis.name: verifyDisabledSchedule (task 1, not yet written)
apis.signature: verifyDisabledSchedule(expected, observed) -> boolean (contract text, plan l.87)
apis.behavior: Contract requires: pure, with no filesystem or network effects. expected = automationSchedulePlan output. observed = {id,name,timeZone,cron,commandArgv,cwd,enabled,exact,noDeliver}. The task 5 worker must READ the actual code and document what it does. The file does not exist at HEAD bbe4575.

apis.name: installDisabledAutomation (task 2, not yet written)
apis.behavior: Contract requires: no implicit production defaults; persist an exclusive per-name intent before any scheduler effect; record the returned id before verifying; publish root/installed/<name>.json in runInstalledAutomation's shape and ledgers via initializeAutomationDispatch(root/runtime); return verified only after publication and read-back. The actual state names and intent path are whatever task 2 wrote, and the doc must quote them from the code.

apis.name: reconcileDisabledAutomation (task 3, not yet written)
apis.behavior: Contract requires: it never creates or enables jobs, never resets quotas, and never presumes a lock owner is dead. A missing returned id stays blocked. Remove is allowed only when transaction identity and read-back match exactly. The actual behaviour is whatever task 3 wrote.

apis.name: workerTurn / renderContract / renderCheckResults
apis.signature: workerTurn({contract, files, checkResults, instructions, turn, maxTurns, attempt, maxAttempts, notice, checkDescriptions, feedback})
apis.behavior: The prompt carries the contract (only the fields at l.43-74, with no commit ids and no other tasks), the brief (l.83-89), files without line numbers (l.91-96), and check results whose output is cut to the last 6,000 characters (l.98-107). No earlier reasoning is carried over (l.14-17).

apis.name: runCheck (per-file and command)
apis.behavior: When no .mjs/.js file changed, node-syntax returns {ok:true, exitCode:0, output:'no matching changed files'} (l.262-264). automation-install-tests runs `node --test tests/automation-install.test.mjs` (l.63-68). automation-tests runs the seven existing suites (l.69-77). Captured output is capped at 60,000 characters (l.138).

apis.name: reviewCheckpoint
apis.signature: async reviewCheckpoint({runtime, worktree, task, baseRef, checkResults, workerSummary, priorFindings, ...})
apis.behavior: Re-runs the checks independently (l.65-82). The reviewer then gets only {name, ok, ms, exitCode} with no output (l.83), plus the diff of this checkpoint only (l.89). reviewerTurn passes no files (prompts.mjs:156-168).

shapes.name: Installed record consumed by runInstalledAutomation
shapes.definition: {name, installationId (/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{8,80}$/), action:'agenda_today', installedAt (ISO string), timeZone (IANA or 'UTC'), expiresOn 'YYYY-MM-DD', permissions:{expectsMode}, conditions:{skipDuringFocus?, quietHours?}, riskLimits:{maxRunsPerDay 1..1440}, failureBehavior, trigger:{kind, atMinute, atHour?, weekday?}}, with no delivery field
shapes.evidence: runtime.mjs:29-31; dispatch.mjs:14-27; admission.mjs:14-29; fixture at tests/automation-runtime.test.mjs:13-16

shapes.name: Dispatch ledger
shapes.definition: <root>/runtime/<sha256hex(installationId)>.dispatch.json = {version:1, binding:sha256(canonical(record)), phase:'ready'|'pending'|'stopped'|'action_completed'|'delivery_pending'|'delivery_unknown', lastAt:null|ms, lastSlot:null|'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM', lastDelivery?}; lock dir <file>.lock

shapes.name: Admission ledger
shapes.definition: <root>/runtime/admission/<sha256hex(installationId)>.json = {version:1, binding, day:null|'YYYY-MM-DD', runs, lastAt}; lock dir <key>.lock, which is never removed automatically

shapes.name: Schedule plan (expected input to verifyDisabledSchedule)
shapes.definition: {readyToInstall:false, nextGate, name, timeZone, cron, commandArgv, policy, schedulerArgs}; the cwd to compare is the element after '--command-cwd' in schedulerArgs (it equals repoRoot)

shapes.name: Observed scheduler object (task 1 contract)
shapes.definition: {id, name, timeZone, cron, commandArgv, cwd, enabled, exact, noDeliver}

shapes.name: Real scheduler list read-back (only evidence in the source)
shapes.definition: `cron list --all --json` gives {jobs:[{id:string, name:string,...}], hasMore:false, offset:0, total:jobs.length}

shapes.name: Check result as the worker sees it
shapes.definition: '### <name> — PASSED|FAILED|TIMED OUT|UNUSABLE ENVIRONMENT (exit N)' then a fenced block holding the last 6,000 characters. Node 26 spec reporter lines look like '✔ <test name> (Nms)', and the summary lines are 'ℹ tests N', 'ℹ suites N', 'ℹ pass N', 'ℹ fail N', 'ℹ cancelled N', 'ℹ skipped N', 'ℹ todo N', 'ℹ duration_ms N'
shapes.evidence: prompts.mjs:98-107; run observed 2026-09-23 on node v26.5.0: existing automation-tests gave 6,954 characters of output and 'ℹ tests 82 / ℹ pass 82 / ℹ fail 0'

shapes.name: Review contract (reviewer output)
shapes.definition: {verdict:PASS|PASS_WITH_TASKS|BLOCKED, summary, examined, passed, failed:[{criterion,severity,evidence}], corrections, escalationReason, escalationKind}

testPatterns.pattern: The fixture shape for installed runtime tests: a temporary root, a hand-written installed record, initializeAutomationDispatch at root/runtime, and injected checks/run. Task 4's contract forbids hand-authoring the record, so its fixture test must produce the record with installDisabledAutomation instead. The doc worker should check which one the install tests actually do.
testPatterns.snippet: const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "orion-runtime-")); ... await initializeAutomationDispatch(join(root, "runtime"), record);

testPatterns.pattern: 'Actual child-process exit at a transaction seam' in this codebase means a node child started with execFile(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module','-e', source]) that calls process.exit(73) partway through. A thrown Error or a rejected promise does not count as an actual process exit.

The existing standard for 'real disposable effect then failure is not retried': a shell script appends to effect.txt and exits 1, and the test asserts outcome_unknown, then 'stopped' on replay, then exactly one effect line.

Citing test evidence in the doc: use the exact test name string from test("...") plus the file path. Do not cite line numbers, because the worker never sees them. Copy the summary lines from CHECK RESULTS exactly as printed.

criteria.criterion: Document public APIs, transaction states, side-effect ordering, durable paths, rollback/reconciliation behavior and invariants actually implemented.
criteria.approach: READ scripts/lib/orion-automation-install.mjs as it stands in the worktree. List every export with its exact signature. List the state/status string literals exactly as spelled. Give the order of steps: intent persisted, scheduler.createDisabled, id recorded, ledgers/record published, read-back and verify, return. Then give durable paths, what reconcile does in each state, and the invariants. Use existing module facts for the shared paths: installed/<name>.json (runtime.mjs:25), runtime/<sha256(installationId)>.dispatch.json (dispatch.mjs:54), runtime/admission/<sha256(installationId)>.json (admission.mjs:43-44,67). Write down the intent-file path as the code defines it. Where the code differs from the task 1–3 contracts, say so explicitly.
criteria.evidence: The install files are the combined output of tasks 1–4 (both absent at HEAD bbe4575; git ls-tree shows nothing). The shared ledger formats are cited at left. Invariants that already exist: the runtime never initializes ledgers (runtime.mjs:1-2; tests/automation-runtime.test.mjs:62-65); no quota refunds (admission.mjs:142-145); locks are never removed automatically (admission.mjs:149-151); 'wx' refuses overwrite (dispatch.mjs:42; admission.mjs:47).
criteria.risk: The most likely wrong version copies the contract text into the doc as if it were implemented, for example saying 'returns verified only after read-back' without checking the code. Another is inventing state names such as 'no_effect' or 'known_disabled' that do not appear in the code. A third is documenting a function evicted from the working set from memory. Any of these would pass a local review, because the reviewer cannot see the source.

criteria.criterion: Map every task acceptance criterion to concrete tests or explicit unproven status; distinguish observed check output from inferred behavior.
criteria.approach: For each of the 19 criteria in tasks 1–4 (the brief must quote them, because the plan is not in the worktree), give the test name(s) in tests/automation-install.test.mjs whose assertions actually exercise it. Label each 'observed' (passing output visible in this task's CHECK RESULTS, or covered by an exact 'ℹ pass N' / 'ℹ fail 0' / 'ℹ skipped 0' / 'ℹ todo 0' summary), 'inferred' (read in source, no test), or 'unproven'. Say that node-syntax passed only because no .mjs/.js file changed. Task 5's own criteria are met by the document itself, not by tests.
criteria.evidence: The plan is untracked (`?? docs/agentic/plans/advance-orion-capabilities.md`), so it is not in the worktree, which is built from HEAD (workspace.mjs:100-123). The worker's contract has only task 5 (prompts.mjs:43-74). Check output is cut to the last 6,000 characters (prompts.mjs:104). node-syntax gives 'no matching changed files' (checks.mjs:262-264).
criteria.risk: Marking every criterion 'covered' because a test name sounds right, for example a 'concurrency' test that runs sequentially or a 'child-process exit' test that only throws. Claiming the admission tests are missing because they were cut from the visible tail. Citing check output from an earlier task that the worker never saw.

criteria.criterion: Identify the remaining real scheduler adapter, explicit human activation, exact installed read-back, remote controls, and disposable live-route proof. Do not say any of these happened in the fixture.
criteria.approach: Make a 'Not done / not proven' section that lists all five items. Evidence for each: CLI install still refuses (scripts/orion-automation:153-157). No enable/activate path exists. The only source evidence of the real read-back format is the list shape in removal.mjs:9-18, which has no enabled/cron/tz/argv/cwd fields, so mapping the real output to the normalized observed object is not established. No automation controls exist in scripts/orion-remote (git grep shows only a TCC comment at l.581). The fixture used a fake scheduler and temporary roots only.
criteria.evidence: scripts/orion-automation:153-157; orion-automation-removal.mjs:9-18; schedule.mjs:29-30 (readyToInstall:false and the nextGate text); `git grep -i automation HEAD -- scripts/orion-remote` gives only l.581
criteria.risk: Wording such as 'verified disabled job' or 'installed' without 'fake scheduler / temporary root'. Describing remote controls as existing. Presenting the fake adapter's read(id) as 'installed read-back'.

criteria.criterion: List changed paths and limitations relevant to Astra review, including crash windows and unknown outcomes. Do not mark Phase 57 complete, edit the manifest or claim installation/deployment.
criteria.approach: Changed paths: scripts/lib/orion-automation-install.mjs, tests/automation-install.test.mjs, and this doc. Say this list is inferred from scope enforcement (boundary.mjs:194-198; repairs keep the task's scope, reviewer.mjs:20-21; corrections cannot widen scope, orion-project-agent.mjs:556-563), not observed from git. Crash windows: take each seam from the install code (before create, after create but before the id is durable, after read-back but before or during publication), plus the dispatch window between reservation and pending (dispatch.mjs:103-108), lock dirs left behind by a crash (dispatch.mjs:66,173; admission.mjs:149-151), and non-atomic check-then-spawn (runtime.mjs:57-66). State that Phase 57 remains in progress, and that commit ids were not supplied to the worker.
criteria.evidence: Scope is enforced at boundary.mjs:194-198. The Phase 57 gate at HEAD is status 'in_progress' (docs/planning/v2/PHASE_GATES.json, entry "57", around l.4695-4697 at HEAD).
criteria.risk: Claiming a per-task diff attribution or commit SHAs. Trying to update PHASE_GATES.json, HANDOFF.md or MANIFEST_PHASES.json (refused, and an exchange wasted). Omitting the crash window between scheduler create and durable id recording, which is the one task 3 exists to handle.

criteria.criterion: State the next bounded source task and the specific live proof required; do not start that work inside this documentation task.
criteria.approach: Use the plan's own follow-on list, quoted in the brief because the plan is not in the worktree. Next source task: item 1, 'Implement the exact installed scheduler adapter: supported argv only, parse current read-back format, create disabled, verify exact identity and fields, refuse unknown schema.' Live proof: item 4, 'Exercise a disposable complete route through the installed scheduler, then stop/remove it and verify absence. No real calendar messages or broad standing routines as a test substitute.' Activation (item 3) is a separate, human-gated step. Write no code.
criteria.evidence: plan l.301-309 (untracked, so the brief must supply it); scope is only the doc (plan l.283-285)
criteria.risk: Inventing a different next task, for example 'enable the job' or 'wire the CLI' first, without saying why. Writing adapter code, which is refused because it is out of scope. Describing the live proof vaguely, for example as 'test with the real scheduler', without remove-and-verify-absence.

issues.detail: Runtime limit specific to a single-file task. After the first write, no more progress is possible unless a check goes from failing to passing, so the fourth exchange that contains FILE, CHECK or DONE, counting the first write, triggers 'stuck' before DONE is handled. The stuck path hands the task to the reviewer for repair and notifies Nick.

issues.recommendedInterpretation: The brief tells the worker to spend at most three exchanges with FILE, CHECK or DONE: a full draft with CHECK, a final version with CHECK (or with DONE), then DONE. Nick may want to know that stuckAfterTurns=4 is tight for documentation tasks.

issues.detail: Correction tasks run before new plan work, but only while they are claimable. If a correction task for task 4 is parked under an escalation, task 5 can still run, because it depends only on the accepted parent. The packet would then describe uncorrected code.

pitfalls: READ with the bare names in the context string ('orion-automation-dispatch.mjs') gives 'Could not read'. Use scripts/lib/orion-automation-dispatch.mjs and the other full paths (workspace.mjs:174-183).
Trying to READ docs/agentic/plans/advance-orion-capabilities.md, which is untracked and so not in the worktree. Rely on the brief's quoted criteria and next-batch list.

READing HANDOFF.md (93,611 characters at HEAD, cut at 90,000, about 31k tokens), docs/planning/v2/PHASE_GATES.json (545,310 characters) or AGENTS.md (47,073) pushes the install files out of the ~48.5k-token budget (context.mjs:74-83). The model is not told when a file is evicted (worker.mjs:161-163 only records it in the journal).
